editorial:
Ever felt so scared of something that you went totally overboard to prepare for it? You will meet a young Japanese boy who is completely terrified of tsunamis. He is so worried about a flood that he actually builds a pair of giant inflatable rubber underpants to keep himself floating. It sounds wild, but the movie takes this weird idea and runs with it. The vibe is strange and a bit awkward, especially when he decides to board a special subway car reserved only for top models. You get a front-row seat to a very odd clash of worlds as this nervous kid enters a room full of high-fashion glamour.

What really works here is how the movie handles the tension. The acting is great, and the way the story builds up to a breaking point keeps you guessing. While the pace is a bit slow at times, the weirdness makes up for it. If you like stories that are a bit off-beat and surprising, you should definitely check this out.
endingExplained: In the end, the boy's fear reaches a boiling point inside the model carriage. The trigger happens, and he finally puts on his rubber underpants in front of everyone. Instead of being mocked, the sheer absurdity of the situation creates a weird bond between him and the models. The movie wraps up by showing that his strange obsession actually helped him break out of his shell and connect with people he never would have talked to otherwise.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves odd stories and quirky characters.
